entries.title: A 'historically' strong El Niño is expected to make for a milder Chicago winter
entries.summary: <p>A potentially "historically strong” El Niño will make for milder winter temperatures in Chicago, according to the National Weather Service’s Winter Outlook report released Thursday.</p><p>An El Niño is a weather event that occurs when abnormally warm water temperatures in the Pacific lead to changes in weather patterns globally, specifically warmer temperatures across northern North America.</p><p>They typically occur every two to seven years. The last was in 2023 into 2024, and the current one has the potential to extend into March 2027.</p><p>“It’s probably just going to feel like any other warmer winter, especially for the latter half of the winter when the effect seems to be maximized,” said Kevin Doom, a meteorologist with the weather service. “That doesn't mean every day will be above average though, we’ll still see periods of harsh cold and wintry precipitation events.”</p><p>For the Chicago area, that means a 50 to 60% chance of above normal temperatures this winter, though the weather service said even in a mild winter to expect “notable” stretches of cold weather and snow storms.</p><p>The predicted El Niño is expected to compete with the one from the winter of 1982-83 — which raised the average winter temperature for the area by five to seven degrees and lowered snowfall by 25 to 50% — for the strongest since 1950, according to the weather service.</p><p>The report also states the weather will make for a stronger jet stream, which should largely keep polar air, the cause of polar vortexes that bring brutal stretches of chilling cold, to a minimum.</p><p>However, the report notes that “no two El Niños are alike and impacts vary.”</p><p>“It’s not a guarantee, but given this one is overly strong, confidence is pretty high [we’ll see higher temperatures],” Doom said. “This is the strongest El Niño we’ve seen in awhile, at least as long as I’ve been around.”</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">[9:57 AM CDT Thursday 10/16/2026]<br>With the release of the official NOAA -
